course_description:
Students will undertake a supervised experiential placement in a pharmacy practice site that promotes opportunities to develop professional pharmacy practice knowledge, skills, and attributes, building on the previous three years of the Pharmacy Program.

PHRM4062 involves an experiential placement over 6 consecutive weeks, 4 days per week, in an Australian community pharmacy. Students will complete their placement in either Semester 1 or Semester 2 of Year 4 of the Program. The placement commences two weeks prior to Week 1 of the semester and concludes at the end of Week 4.

This capstone course offers a unique opportunity for the student to further expand their professional practice experience in preparation for graduation and beyond, the internship year and achievement of full professional competence. The student will complete a minimum of 180 hours of supervised community pharmacy experiential placement, reflect on their individual practice from personal and professional angles (i.e. relate it to specific elements of the National Competency Standards for Pharmacists in Australia 2016), and provide reflection and feedback on their overall learning across the 4 years of their degree and into the future, as they continue their professional development as lifelong learners. During their placement experiences, students will also undertake a range of Entrustable Professional Activities relevant to their placement site under supervision by their preceptor.

Students are encouraged to consider their wellbeing during the placement, ranging from developing basic awareness of safety matters (e.g. arranging safe travel to and from the placement site) to active self-care and looking after their health and wellbeing during their placement. Student wellbeing during placement is not only important in relation to the UQ Placements Policy, but is also absolutely essential for effective learning, overall professionalisation, and a happy, healthy and balanced life.

course_aims: The overall aim of this placement course is for final-year pharmacy students to acquire a wholesome and informative experience of professional practice in an Australian community pharmacy over 6 consecutive weeks, 4 days per week. This capstone placement course is an opportunity for students to build holistically on their previous experiences, reflect on their personal and professional progress, acknowledge with clarity their current strengths and weaknesses as practitioners-in-training at this point in time, and start meaningfully considering their personal and professional development as lifelong learners.

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate reflective practice, professional competence, interpersonal skills and expertise in the Australian community pharmacy setting; including the development of learning plans for experiential placements
Relate your knowledge, skills, and professional attributes acquired throughout the Pharmacy degree in the context of your placement experience

Reflect on your placement experience and relate it to your personal and professional development, including in the context of the National Competency Standards Framework for Pharmacists in Australia 2016, life-long learning, and future employability
Start your continuing professional development by reflecting on your past and present experiences and your future as a lifelong learner

assessment_details.title: Placement Participation, Entrustable Professional Activities (EPAs), EPA Reflection and Individual Learning Plan (ILP)
assessment_details.other_conditions: Work integrated learning, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: PLACEMENT PARTICIPATION Each student must attend and complete their placement for 6 consecutive weeks, 4 days per week and at least 180 hours , in their placement pharmacy, commencing two weeks prior to Week 1 of semester and concluding at the end of Week 4. Any alterations to the set timeframe must be discussed with and approved by the Course Coordinator prior to the placement. The start and finish time each day will depend on the agreement between the student and their preceptor. If the placement includes a public holiday relevant to that placement site, the students are expected to attend/not attend the placement site in accordance with usual practice at that site, e.g. if the facility is not open during the public holiday, then the students do not attend and that time is included within the 180 hours. In the case of illness, students are NOT expected to attend their placement and should inform their preceptor. Absences should be recorded in InPlace within 24 hours of your absence ( instructions here ). Students away from their placement site for more than TWO days due to illness (i.e. on the third day) should obtain a medical certificate and provide this to the School Office and their preceptor. Students are advised to contact the Course Coordinator to report any prolonged absence (more than THREE days) from the placement site due to illness. Additionally, irrespective of medical certificates, any cumulative absence of longer than 3 days over the 6-week period must be immediately brought to the attention of the Course Coordinator. All students are expected to be available to commence classes in other Year 4 courses in Week 5 of semester. ENTRUSTABLE PROFESSIONAL ACTIVITIES (EPAs) Evidence of entrustment discussions with your preceptor during placement and final entrustment decision at the end of your placement should be completed via the ePortfolio. Students will choose a minimum of THREE (3) EPAs from the suite of provided EPAs that are relevant to the placement site and the students’ learning goals. Students are required to submit a statement of justification for their choice of EPAs with their EPA self-assessment. See the Learn.UQ (Blackboard) site for more information regarding the EPAs. EPA REFLECTION and INDIVIDUAL LEARNING PLAN (ILP) After the placement period is complete, students are required to complete their Reflection and Individual Learning Plan (ILP) for submission via the ePortfolio, based on the feedback they have received from their preceptor or other colleagues at the placement site, the entrustment levels assigned for each EPA undertaken and the action plan discussed during the final feedback session with the preceptor. See Learn.UQ (Blackboard) for more information and marking criteria. Student Reflection: This should be uploaded as a separate WORD.doc file in the ePortfolio . The maximum word count for the student reflection is 500 words. Students can use the SEAL reflection template if they wish, but can also follow a more generalised structure to reflect on their overall experience in undertaking the chosen EPAs during their placement. It is important for students to focus on their learnings, linking actions to their future development. Students can include references or attachments where necessary/appropriate to support their reflection. Individual Learning Plan (ILP): The ePortfolio provides clear instructions and a template for students to complete their ILP based on their performance in undertaking the EPAs and feedback from their preceptor during their placement. Students should complete each of the relevant boxes in the template prior to submission. Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools may be used appropriately to support students in completing this assessment task. Students must clearly acknowledge any use of AI in each instance. A failure to acknowledge generative AI use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Read full task description Hide full task description

Submission: The EPA self-reflections, EPA Reflection and ILP are submitted via the ePortfolio by the due date. The completed EPA self-reflections will be submitted to the student's preceptor via ePortfolio. This will trigger an email to be sent to the Preceptor with a link to complete the student's final EPA entrustment levels and confirm the student's attendance at the placement site via the ePortfolio.
Resubmission: Students who do not meet the required pass criteria will be given one opportunity to resubmit the assessment.
Deferral or extension
You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 28 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
Late submission

You will receive a mark of FAIL if this assessment is submitted late without an approved extension.

assessment_details.title: SEAL Reflections
assessment_details.due_date: SEAL Submission 1: 2 x NCS Schema 11/09/2026 5:00 pm SEAL Submission 2: 1 x LLL Schema + 1 x Employability Schema 23/10/2026 5:00 pm
assessment_details.task_description: Students will submit a total of FOUR reflections: SEAL Submission 1: 2 x 500 words for EACH NCS Schema (total ~1000 words) SEAL Submission 2: 1 x 500 words LLL Schema + 1 x 500 words Employability Schema (total ~1000 words) These reflections are a significant part of this course, and students are expected to provide a high standard of reflection for each submission. The key component of reflection is ensuring the creation of a specific plan to aid learning within the scope of the situation, and describing how this action is being undertaken. Each reflection should not exceed 500 words. More information and marking rubrics for the SEAL reflections can be found on Learn.UQ (Blackboard) on the Assessment page. Students should consider their individual experiences during their Placement in order to reflect effectively within each of the different schemas described below: 1. National Competency Standards (NCS) schema: Please read the relevant National Competency Standards (NCS) Framework for Pharmacists in Australia 2016 (available through the course Blackboard site) and familiarise yourself with the Standards before attending your placement. Students are to reflect on ONE chosen Enabling Competency from the NCS in each reflection. Each selected Enabling Competency should be different from the others. Students should reflect on the level of skills, knowledge or professional attributes they acquired/demonstrated during their placement experience and relate this clearly to the chosen Enabling Competency. Students are also encouraged to reflect on their own unique personal experiences (e.g. feelings, personal attributes, individual strengths/weaknesses at this stage of development, etc). 2. Lifelong Learning (LLL) schema : Students should reflect on their own future learning needs and how they have used feedback to inform their ongoing development, which will enable them to professionally manage their internship and joining the pharmacy profession. They should focus on how their placement uncovered specific elements of their own practice and learning that they consider to be particularly relevant to their future practice, and for becoming a lifelong learner who will remain committed to their continuing professional development. Students should focus on reflecting on ONE or TWO experiences that highlighted the evolving nature of the pharmacy industry and how the experience has highlighted specific gaps in their own knowledge or development, focusing on a clear learning plan to bridge the gaps identified from the experience, and consider how they can plan to maintain ongoing lifelong learning throughout their careers. 3. Employability schema : Employability can be defined as a “ set of capabilities and personal attributes that empower graduates to perform effectively in the workplace, generate opportunities, and create positive social and economic impact” . This Employability Reflection is an opportunity for students to reflect on their own personal experiences in relation to any aspects of their individual employability at this late stage of their student career path. It is strongly recommended that, before their placement, students familiarise themselves with UQ’s Employability Framework for necessary background information on the meaning, definitions, structure, and relevant considerations in preparation for addressing this assessment item: https://employability.uq.edu.au/about/employability-framework. In this schema, students should focus on personal or professional attributes (rather than clinical skills or knowledge) that can be further developed to aid future employability for their internship and onwards. Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools may be used appropriately to support students in completing this assessment task. Students must clearly acknowledge any use of AI in each instance. A failure to acknowledge generative AI use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Read full task description Hide full task description

learning_activities.topic: Online Module - Course Introduction The Course Introduction module can be completed by students anytime prior to the commencement of their placement. It can be accessed online via the course Learn.UQ site. It relays important information about the placement and assessment expectations. There is a short quiz made up of 10 multiple choice questions following the completion of the module. You must achieve at least 80% on the quiz, and you are allowed multiple attempts. The quiz does not count towards your course grade. The module will cover the following: Introduction to PHRM4062 Placements Assessment overview and expectations Entrustable Professional Activities (EPAs) and Individual Learning Plan You must complete this module and successfully pass the quiz before you can access the Assessments folder. This will allow you to access the assessment submission links as well as information regarding course assessments. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Online Introductory Lecture Online Introductory Lecture: The Course Coordinator will provide a course introduction, an overview of the placement and work-integrated learning, and give guidance on how to perform productively and successfully in this course. The lecture will be an opportunity for students to ask questions and clarify any concerns prior to commencing their placements. The online lecture will take place approximately two weeks before placements commence. This Lecture will be held online on Tuesday, 30th June 2026 at 1pm - See Learn.UQ (Blackboard) Announcements for the Zoom link. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
